decisions.rationale: Valid, medium. Same root cause as ops-sme-010. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r2 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at 8e30c874 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 111e75f2), with npm ci in tests and Node v24.2.0. The shipped starter fails 26/26, and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's own solution, written from the README, the topic pages and the public tests, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. Each variant named below is a one-change edit of that solution, run the same way. No private overlay, private staging or author work folder was read. Two variants each fail only test 25: the URL moved into a local variable passed to httpx.get, with a dict-literal headers argument, and the same with a named headers dict. The message is "send the incoming authorization value on as the outgoing Authorization header of the call to the shop api", although the header is forwarded. The page's own async shape (url variable, named headers, named Timeout on an AsyncClient get) fails test 25 the same way. outgoingCall (tests/lab.mjs lines 311-322) takes the first call whose own argument text contains API_BASE_URL, so a URL built on an earlier line leaves no call. Acceptance: reviews-auth-forward meets the call list in the ops-sme-010 decision of this file: c2, c3 and c6 pass, all must-fail shapes fail, and a missing call gets the no-call message instead of the header message. Grader or message change only: no new learner task, objective, time or architecture, within the operator's option A for ops-lab-loop3.

Valid, low. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r2 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at 8e30c874 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 111e75f2), with npm ci in tests and Node v24.2.0. The reconciler's own solution, written from the README, the topic pages and the public tests, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT. Each variant named below is a one-change edit of that solution, run the same way. No private overlay, private staging or author work folder was read. (a) The guard rewritten with detail first and status_code=401 second fails test 25 with "your missing-token check does not raise HTTPException with 401". RAISE_401 (line 335) reads 401 only directly after the opening parenthesis, while handlers() (line 364) already takes the status in either order. (b) A positive check wrapping the call, with 401 raised in else, fails with "a request with no token would reach the shop api without one". So does the SME's shape: headers built under the positive check, else raising 401, and the call after the if/else. Line 349 recognises only negative guards. A positive check with no else, and one whose else returns a dict, both fail today and must keep failing. Acceptance: the guard list. Guard list. Must pass reviews-auth-forward, given the call-list forward: (g1) a not-authorization guard before the call that raises HTTPException with 401 as status_code first; (g2) the same with detail first and status_code=401 after it; (g3) 401 given positionally, or as the status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED constant; (g4) an is-None or ==-None guard; (g5) a positive check (if authorization:, or is not None) whose body holds the outgoing call and whose else branch raises HTTPException with 401; (g6) a positive check that builds the headers in its body, with an else branch that raises 401 and the call after the whole if/else; (g7) a required authorization parameter with no guard. Must fail: (f1) a guard body that only prints; (f2) an HTTPException created without raise; (f3) a guard that returns a dict; (f4) the guard removed, with the headers conditional on authorization, inline or through a name; (f5) a forwarding dict built but not passed, with the call sending an empty headers dict; (f6) a positive check with no else, so nothing answers 401; (f7) a positive check whose else returns a dict instead of raising 401; (f8) a not-authorization guard placed after the call. f1-f3 and f7 get a message that names the missing raise and is true for the shape. The current text, "so the request still goes on to the call", is false for f3 and f7, which return before the call. f4, f6 and the no-guard dict-literal shape get the no-guard message, worded as in ops-sme-r2-01. This closed list replaces the universal sentences of earlier acceptances for this item. Shapes outside it are non-binding: they may pass, or fail with a message that is true for them. Grader or message change only: no new learner task, objective, time or architecture, within the operator's option A for ops-lab-loop3.

The message does not say "without --host" and does not state who can reach that address, so the ops-edu-r1-01 listen-address item stays resolved. uvicorn with no --host option fails with the existing wording about a missing --host. uvicorn with the all-interfaces host the adding-FastAPI page gives still passes. Both no-guard shapes fail test 25 with "a request with no token would reach the shop api without one". The first is a dict literal mapping Authorization to the optional parameter, with no guard. The second is the headers made conditional on authorization. For the dict-literal shape the claim is false. The reconciler had no httpx in its scratch environment and did not execute it. It relies on two executed records: the SME critic's FastAPI TestClient run (httpx 0.28.1 raises TypeError on a None header value before any request, the caller gets 500, and the stub api receives nothing), and the earlier reconciliation's ops-edu-06 venv check, which shows the same TypeError. For the conditional shape the claim is true. Restoring the loop-1 wording verbatim, as decision-loop3.md item 3 says, would be false for the conditional shape instead. Acceptance: the no-guard message is true for both shapes. Either it states only what holds for both (for example, that nothing answers 401 before the call when authorization is missing, so the request ends in a 500 or reaches the shop api without a token), or it is chosen by whether the headers expression is conditional. The guard list's must-fail shapes keep failing. Checked by reading the message text against both shapes. With a least-access top-level block in place, two one-change variants pass 26/26 even though they give the build job, which holds the registry secrets, a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN: the build job given permissions: write-all, and the build job given contents: read plus packages: write. ci-permissions returns as soon as a top-level block exists (line 586), and GitHub documents that a job-level permissions key sets that job's token access (SME critic evidence). Acceptance: when a top-level block exists, ci-permissions also applies the same least-access rule to every job that has its own permissions block, and fails with the existing least-access messages. Must fail: both variants above, plus the existing cases (a top-level string such as write-all, a top-level packages write). Must pass: the top-level block alone; the top-level block plus a job block of contents: read only (passes today and must keep passing); the per-job-only path from ops-sme-r1-04 unchanged. Valid, low. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-r2 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at 8e30c874 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 111e75f2), with npm ci in tests and Node v24.2.0. Each variant named below is a one-change edit of that solution, run the same way. No private overlay, private staging or author work folder was read. A new build-job step whose run block is cat with an unquoted heredoc whose body is the job-env variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD passes 26/26. So does the <<- form, and so does a heredoc with a quoted delimiter whose body is the secrets-context expression; GitHub substitutes that expression before the shell runs. The reconciler ran the shapes under bash -e (3.2.57) with a dummy value and a stub docker. Both the unquoted and the <<- heredoc write the value to the output. A quoted-delimiter heredoc holding only the shell variable does not, and neither does a heredoc fed to docker login --password-stdin. commands() (lines 508-511) splits on newlines, so the body line is judged apart from cat. Acceptance: ci-no-secret-prints folds each heredoc body, from a <<WORD or <<-WORD operator to its terminator, into the command that opened it. Must fail, for a heredoc opened by cat: (h1) the unquoted heredoc above; (h2) the <<- form; (h3) a quoted or unquoted body that holds a secrets-context expression, or an env-context expression of a secret-mapped name. Not flagged by ci-no-secret-prints: (h4) a cat heredoc with a quoted delimiter whose body holds only the shell variable; (h5) a heredoc fed to docker login --password-stdin, whatever its body. ci-secret-refs may still fail h5 with its honest piped-form message. h5 takes precedence over h3. Heredocs opened by any other command are non-binding. The existing test 7 message stays true for h1-h3. This closed list replaces the universal sentences of earlier acceptances for this item. Shapes outside it are non-binding: they may pass, or fail with a message that is true for them. Two shapes pass 26/26 although the request runs on HTTPX defaults: (a) an unused module-level httpx client built with a valid Timeout, while the httpx.get call has no timeout; (b) a local helper function that takes a timeout parameter, called with the Timeout before the request, while the httpx.get call has none. A print call carrying the keyword also passes the grader, but Python's print rejects a timeout keyword, so only the helper form is runnable. keywordArgs and line 286 count a timeout keyword on any call except httpx.Timeout itself. The same scan also reads a def's timeout=None parameter default as a call passing None. A helper declared that way fails with the false message "the call passes timeout=None". Counting only on the outgoing call removes this too. Acceptance: reviews-timeouts counts a timeout only on the outgoing call identified by the call list (see ops-sme-010 in this file), or on the constructor of the client that makes that call. Must fail: (a) and (b), with the existing built-but-never-used message or a message equally true; the unused lowercase local named timeout with no timeout on the call; the same with a plain number on the call (single-number message); an unused Timeout under another name; read=None and connect=None; timeout=None on the call, even when its client carries a valid Timeout. Must pass: an otherwise correct solution that also has an unrelated def with a timeout=None parameter default; a Timeout inline in the call; one bound to a module-level name and passed by that name; one bound to a local named timeout and passed by it; one given to the constructor of the httpx client that makes the call (call-list shapes c4 and c5); the page's shape c6; and c2, the URL in a variable. These forwarding shapes fail only test 25 with the false header message: the URL in a local variable (with a dict literal and with a named dict); a module-level base_url client whose get takes a relative path; an earlier print line that mentions API_BASE_URL; and the page's own async shape. The with-block client (c5) passes today. Acceptance: Outgoing-call list (call list). Locate the outgoing request by callee, not by where the API_BASE_URL text appears. The callee is an httpx module verb (get, post, put, patch, delete, head, options, request, stream) or the same verb on a name bound to an httpx Client or AsyncClient, whether by assignment or by a with or async with ... as clause. Calls to os.environ.get, getenv, print and logging functions are never taken as the outgoing call. The forwarded header and the timeout are read only from that call's own arguments or from the constructor of the client that makes it. Must pass reviews-auth-forward, when the guard and the forward are otherwise correct: (c1) the URL f-string inline in an httpx.get call; (c2) the URL built in a local variable on an earlier line and passed to httpx.get, with a dict-literal headers argument; (c3) the same with a headers dict bound to a name; (c4) a module-level httpx client built with base_url set to API_BASE_URL and a Timeout, whose get takes a relative path and the headers; (c5) a with-block httpx client built with the Timeout, whose get makes the call; (c6) the service-to-service page's own shape (artifact.md lines 23-25): an async handler, an async-with AsyncClient, a url variable, a named headers dict and a named Timeout passed on the awaited get; (c7) any of c1-c6 with an earlier print or log call that mentions API_BASE_URL. The forms already accepted also stay passing: a lowercase header key, a subscript-built dict, and a required authorization parameter with no guard. The ops-edu-06 form, an empty dict filled by subscript under a positive authorization check, counts as the forward only. With the optional parameter it still needs a guard-list 401 path. Reproduced: after a not-authorization 401 guard it passes 26/26; without one it fails only test 25 with the no-guard message, and it must keep failing. Must fail: the five ops-edu-r1-02 variants, see the guard list. When no outgoing httpx call is found, the message says that no httpx call to the shop api was found. It does not name the Authorization header. This closed list replaces the universal sentences of earlier acceptances for this item. Shapes outside it are non-binding: they may pass, or fail with a message that is true for them. The three-stage login (printf of the password variable, then tr -d, then docker login --password-stdin) fails test 6 with "feed the password to docker login through --password-stdin". It fails test 7 with "a run step writes a secret ... to the run log". Under bash -e with a dummy value and a stub docker, the value reaches only docker's stdin and nothing is printed, so both messages are false. intoLogin (line 569) needs exactly two stages, and line 537 takes the second stage as the login. A middle tee /dev/stderr stage does print the value under bash, and test 7 fails it today. That must stay. Acceptance: Login-pipeline list (pipeline list). After backslash and trailing-pipe joining, a command whose last pipe stage is docker login ... --password-stdin is a login pipeline, of any length. Its first stage is the feed that ci-secret-refs checks for the REGISTRY_PASSWORD-mapped variable, and its last stage carries the username variable. Must pass both ci-secret-refs and ci-no-secret-prints: (p1) the README's two-stage form; (p2) a three-stage form, printf of the password variable, then tr -d, then docker login --password-stdin; (p3) the wrapped forms that pass today: a trailing backslash, a line break after the pipe and a trailing || exit 1 (each reproduced 26/26), and a folded block (per the loop-2 SME recheck). Must fail ci-no-secret-prints: (q1) a middle tee /dev/stderr stage before docker login --password-stdin; (q2) the existing encoder and printer forms: echo or printf of a secret-mapped variable into base64, a here-string into base64 or xxd, and the env-context forms of ops-edu-04. Must fail ci-secret-refs: the ops-sme-005 cases (a literal password, -p and --password in any spelling, the login step deleted), and a here-string or redirect feed, with the honest piped-form message. Non-binding: other middle stages that write to the log by themselves, for example through a 2>&1 redirect. This closed list replaces the universal sentences of earlier acceptances for this item. Shapes outside it are non-binding: they may pass, or fail with a message that is true for them. Still open after loop 2 on one of six items: the derived-value question of secrets_in_logs (decisions.yaml lines 88-90). The other five are resolved per the loop-2 education recheck. The reconciler replayed the shipped starter run and read every rule message. The test 7 message prints on the starter run and on the README end-of-S38 checkpoint run, because the pipeline is untouched until phase 6. It reads "(directly, through an env variable or encoded)" and "why a workflow never prints one". Two of the three listed options are contradicted by that wording, one by "encoded" and one by "never prints one", so one option is left. Acceptance: (1) those two options are replaced in place, so the expected option, the field name, its reread hint, the grader's expected value and that option's position in the list stay unchanged, and the ops-edu-r1-03 position balance holds. (2) Each replacement is a concept the secrets page teaches that, by the page, does not keep a derived value out of the log, so the item keeps exactly one defensible answer. (3) No replacement is stated, ruled out or singled out by text the learner reads before answering: the README through phase 7, starter comments and docstrings, test titles, every message printed by the shipped starter run and the end-of-S38 checkpoint run, and the loop-3 wording of test 7. Candidates the reconciler checked against that text: relying on GitHub's automatic redaction of registered secrets (secrets page line 29; no printed message characterises redaction); restricting GITHUB_TOKEN with a permissions block (lines 20-27; the ci-permissions messages describe token access only); limiting the step to same-repository runs (line 37). Excluded: routing the value through a step env variable (line 13), because test 7's "through an env variable" contradicts it; and registering the value as a repository secret, which line 29's redaction of registered secrets makes partly defensible. The author may pick other candidates that meet (2) and (3). (4) Loop-3 edits to the test 7 message, such as the heredoc rule, keep it from characterising how the secrets page treats redaction, derived values or fork runs. Non-binding residual: the two test 24 messages at tests/lab.mjs lines 292 and 296 describe what a None limit does. They print only after the learner has already put a None into httpx.Timeout, and the listen-address-and-timeout item they bear on was ruled resolved in loop 2. The education critic verifies by replaying the starter and checkpoint runs. A starter byte change re-records the starter run, both solved overlays and the critic bindings. Test titles and the expected/ summaries do not change. Wording only; no learner time.
